core_obligations: Reduce the adjointness statement to the cited module lemma of the same chapter (proof lines 659-660).
Extend the fibre product diagrams of rings and of modules by their kernels and prove that J maps isomorphically to I and that L maps isomorphically to K (proof lines 661-684).
Show JN' = L by generating L from the images of the products x n' with x in I and n' in N', and deduce N' tensor over B' with B equals N (proof lines 685-694).

Construct the map gamma from N' tensor over B' with A' to M', show it is surjective, compute the kernel of the composite to M as generated by the elements l tensor 1 and n' tensor x, reduce every such element to the form l tensor 1 by the identification JN' = L, and conclude that gamma is injective, hence an isomorphism, so the composition with the original functor is the identity (proof lines 695-712).

The nearest public record in this low range is 305 (806-889, patching equivalence for flat modules over a fibre product), which is the next statement of the same section after this one, and 304 (194-245, tag 07VE, Artin-Rees controlled perturbation). The comparison is therefore between two consecutive statements of the same section, not between duplicates: public 305 is about patching of flat modules and this card is about the right adjoint of the base change functor.
difficulty_reason: The lemma sits inside a Situation with a fibre product of rings and describes the right adjoint of the functor that sends a pair (N, M') to the pair (N tensor B', N tensor A') equipped with its comparison map: the right adjoint is the fibre product N x_M M' over the common quotient M = M'/IM' (statement lines 643-655). It also asserts that the composition with the original functor is the identity, which is the part that has to be proved. The proof is a genuine 58-line sequence of twelve numbered observations (proof lines 658-715): it introduces two new fibre product diagrams with kernels I, J, K, L, proves J maps isomorphically to I and L to K, shows JN' = L, deduces N' tensor B' = N, builds and identifies the map gamma from N' tensor A' to M', computes its kernel, and concludes that gamma is injective, hence an isomorphism. The adjointness half alone is delegated to another lemma of the same chapter, while the identity statement is carried out completely inside the counted span.
